newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open unchanged.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open unchanged.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open unchanged Friday, dealers said.
Thursday, New York arabica futures ended higher but volume was moderate with a lack of follow through from Wednesday's sharp gains on the back of lower than expected Green Coffee Association stocks.
CSCE spot May coffee ended 1.75 cents higher at 209.80 cents a lb, traded 206.10 to 211.50 cents. Most-active July went out 2.20 cents higher at 187.50 cents.

LIFFE coffee futures remained higher at midsession Friday. May rose to a session high of $1,650 a tonne but ran into origin selling, mainly from Indonesia. LIFFE May coffee ended the morning $20 higher at $1,640.
Technically, traders pegged CSCE May resistance at 220 to 230 cents, with support at 180 to 200 cents.
Late Thursday, talks between Brazilian stevedores and steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Paulista failed to resolve a labor dispute at the root of a strike at Santos port, the company said.
A new meeting was set for Friday at 0900 local for talks to resume, the company added.
Brazil's two key coffee ports after Santos are expected to be hit by a 48-hour national strike by stevedores due to begin at 0700 local/1000 GMT Friday, unions said.
Meanwhile the Economist Intelligence Unit cut its estimate of Brazil's 1997/98 exportable coffee production to 16 million 60-kg bags from its earlier forecast of 17.5 million.
It also revised downward the 1996/97 exportable crop for Brazil to 15.3 million bags from 16.8 million.
